Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem.  
Each recursive call works on a smaller piece of the problem, and the process repeats until it reaches a simple case that can be solved directly—called the base case.  
When the base case is reached, the function stops calling itself and the results from each call are combined as the recursion “unwinds” back up the call stack.  
This allows complex tasks, like traversing a tree or calculating factorials, to be expressed in a clear, compact way using the same logic at every level.
